references.text: The entire passage describes the sacrifices for the Feast of Tabernacles (Sukkot), where the number of bulls decreases each day from 13 to 7, while the number of rams and lambs remains constant.
The second day of the Feast of Tabernacles with 12 bulls, illustrating the daily pattern in which one bull is subtracted each day.
The fourth day of the Feast of Tabernacles with 10 bulls, continuing the pattern of a decreasing number of bulls.
The requirement that the sacrificial animals must be without blemish (תְּמִימִם) is repeated here as in other sacrifice regulations.
Basic regulations for the Feast of Tabernacles, which lasts seven days, where Numbers 29 gives detailed provisions for sacrifices.
Ezra mentions the celebration of the Feast of Tabernacles with the daily burnt offerings according to the regulation, referring to the provisions in Numbers 29.
